claim: The eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2α (eIF2α) kinase GCN2 is activated by amino acid starvation to elicit a rectifying physiological program known as the Integrated Stress Response (ISR).
source: The eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2α (eIF2α) kinase GCN2 is activated by amino acid starvation to elicit a rectifying physiological program known as the Integrated Stress Response (ISR).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by the manuscript's introduction and background context.

claim: A role for uncharged tRNAs as activating ligands of yeast GCN2 is supported experimentally.
source: A role for uncharged tRNAs as activating ligands of yeast GCN2 is supported experimentally.
evidence: This claim references experimental support from prior work, as elaborated in the introduction.

claim: Mouse GCN2 activation has recently been observed in circumstances associated with ribosome stalling with no global increase in uncharged tRNAs.
source: However, mouse GCN2 activation has recently been observed in circumstances associated with ribosome stalling with no global increase in uncharged tRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by citation to recent literature, specifically the work of Ishimura et al., 2016 mentioned later in the manuscript.

claim: Disruption of genes encoding components of the ribosome P-stalk, uL10 and P1, selectively attenuated GCN2-mediated ISR activation by amino acid starvation or interference with tRNA charging.
source: Disruption of genes encoding components of the ribosome P-stalk, uL10 and P1, selectively attenuated GCN2-mediated ISR activation by amino acid starvation or interference with tRNA charging without affecting the endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein stress-induced ISR, mediated by the related eIF2α kinase PERK.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the CRISPR screen and subsequent validation experiments shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Disruption of P-stalk genes did not affect the endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein stress-induced ISR, mediated by the related eIF2α kinase PERK.
source: Disruption of genes encoding components of the ribosome P-stalk, uL10 and P1, selectively attenuated GCN2-mediated ISR activation by amino acid starvation or interference with tRNA charging without affecting the endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein stress-induced ISR, mediated by the related eIF2α kinase PERK.
evidence: This selectivity is demonstrated in the flow cytometry data showing preserved XBP1::mCherry and tunicamycin responses in P-stalk mutants (Figures 2A, 3C, 3F).

claim: Wildtype ribosomes isolated from CHO cells stimulated GCN2-dependent eIF2α phosphorylation in vitro.
source: Wildtype ribosomes isolated from CHO cells, but not those with P-stalk lesions, stimulated GCN2-dependent eIF2α phosphorylation in vitro.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 5.

claim: Ribosomes with P-stalk lesions did not stimulate GCN2-dependent eIF2α phosphorylation in vitro.
source: Wildtype ribosomes isolated from CHO cells, but not those with P-stalk lesions, stimulated GCN2-dependent eIF2α phosphorylation in vitro.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the in vitro kinase assays comparing wildtype and mutant ribosomes in Figure 5.

claim: Phosphorylation of translation initiation factor 2 on serine 51 of its alpha subunit (eIF2α) is a potent mechanism for translational regulation in eukaryotes.
source: Phosphorylation of translation initiation factor 2 on serine 51 of its alpha subunit (eIF2α) is a potent mechanism for translational regulation in eukaryotes.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of translation regulation.

claim: Phosphorylated eIF2 impedes the guanine nucleotide exchange activity of eIF2B thereby limiting the pool of active GTP-bound eIF2.
source: Phosphorylated eIF2 impedes the guanine nucleotide exchange activity of eIF2B thereby limiting the pool of active GTP-bound eIF2.
evidence: This is a well-established mechanism in the field.

claim: Levels of eIF2α phosphorylation modulate gene expression translationally and transcriptionally.
source: By way of this direct effect on protein synthesis and its indirect consequences to the abundance of downstream effector proteins, levels of eIF2α phosphorylation modulate gene expression translationally and transcriptionally (Hinnebusch, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hinnebusch, 2014.

claim: In animals four different kinases couple unrelated stress signals to eIF2α phosphorylation.
source: In animals four different kinases couple unrelated stress signals to eIF2α phosphorylation (eIF2αP).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the ISR pathway.

claim: eIF2α phosphorylation effectively integrates stress signals into a stereotypical downstream response referred to as the Integrated Stress Response (ISR).
source: eIF2αP effectively integrates these into a stereotypical downstream response referred to as the Integrated Stress Response (ISR) (Harding et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Harding et al., 2003.

claim: The ISR modulates biological processes ranging from the cell autonomous endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response to organismal immunity, memory and cognition.
source: The ISR modulates biological processes ranging from the cell autonomous endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response to organismal immunity, memory and cognition (Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016; Wek, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016 and Wek, 2018.

claim: The four eIF2a kinases, GCN2, PERK, PKR and HRI, share a similar kinase effector domain.
source: The four eIF2a kinases, GCN2, PERK, PKR and HRI, share a similar kinase effector domain, but diverge in the molecular mechanisms and nature of the upstream signals that regulate their kinase activities.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the structural organization of eIF2α kinases.

claim: The four eIF2a kinases diverge in the molecular mechanisms and nature of the upstream signals that regulate their kinase activities.
source: The four eIF2a kinases, GCN2, PERK, PKR and HRI, share a similar kinase effector domain, but diverge in the molecular mechanisms and nature of the upstream signals that regulate their kinase activities.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the functional diversity of eIF2α kinases.

claim: General Control Non-depressible 2 (GCN2) is the oldest eIF2α kinase, conserved in all known eukaryotes.
source: General Control Non-depressible 2 (GCN2) is the oldest eIF2α kinase, conserved in all known eukaryotes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the evolutionary conservation of GCN2.

claim: GCN2 was discovered as the product of a gene required for yeast adaptation to starvation for any amino acid.
source: It was discovered as the product of a gene required for yeast adaptation to starvation for any amino acid, as in its absence yeast were unable to mount a rectifying transcriptional General Control response (the yeast counterpart to animal cell ISR) (Hinnebusch and Fink, 1983).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hinnebusch and Fink, 1983.

claim: In the absence of GCN2, yeast were unable to mount a rectifying transcriptional General Control response.
source: It was discovered as the product of a gene required for yeast adaptation to starvation for any amino acid, as in its absence yeast were unable to mount a rectifying transcriptional General Control response (the yeast counterpart to animal cell ISR) (Hinnebusch and Fink, 1983).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hinnebusch and Fink, 1983.

claim: The yeast General Control response is the counterpart to animal cell ISR.
source: It was discovered as the product of a gene required for yeast adaptation to starvation for any amino acid, as in its absence yeast were unable to mount a rectifying transcriptional General Control response (the yeast counterpart to animal cell ISR) (Hinnebusch and Fink, 1983).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hinnebusch and Fink, 1983.

claim: The amino acid starvation-induced, GCN2-dependent unicellular gene expression program has as its targets genes encoding transporters and biosynthetic enzymes that function to restore amino acid sufficiency.
source: This amino acid starvation-induced, GCN2-dependent unicellular gene expression program has as its targets genes encoding transporters and biosynthetic enzymes that function to restore amino acid sufficiency, as well as tRNA synthetases that promote amino acid utilization as building blocks of proteins (Hinnebusch, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hinnebusch, 2005.

claim: The amino acid starvation-induced, GCN2-dependent gene expression program targets tRNA synthetases that promote amino acid utilization as building blocks of proteins.
source: This amino acid starvation-induced, GCN2-dependent unicellular gene expression program has as its targets genes encoding transporters and biosynthetic enzymes that function to restore amino acid sufficiency, as well as tRNA synthetases that promote amino acid utilization as building blocks of proteins (Hinnebusch, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hinnebusch, 2005.

claim: GCN2 protein includes an eIF2α kinase module and a module highly related to histidyl-tRNA synthetases (HisRS-like).
source: These physiological features, in conjunction with the domain organization of the GCN2 protein (including an eIF2α kinase module and a module highly related to histidyl-tRNA synthetases, HisRS-like), suggested that uncharged tRNAs may serve as activating ligands of GCN2 as part of a feed-back mechanism that defends cellular pools of charged tRNAs (Wek et al., 1989; Wek et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wek et al., 1989 and Wek et al., 1990.

claim: Uncharged tRNAs may serve as activating ligands of GCN2 as part of a feed-back mechanism that defends cellular pools of charged tRNAs.
source: These physiological features, in conjunction with the domain organization of the GCN2 protein (including an eIF2α kinase module and a module highly related to histidyl-tRNA synthetases, HisRS-like), suggested that uncharged tRNAs may serve as activating ligands of GCN2 as part of a feed-back mechanism that defends cellular pools of charged tRNAs (Wek et al., 1989; Wek et al., 1990).
evidence: This is a model supported by citations to Wek et al., 1989 and Wek et al., 1990.

claim: Mutations in the HisRS-like module that interfere with uncharged tRNA-binding in vitro abolished GCN2 activity in yeast.
source: This model was supported by the observations that mutations in the HisRS-like module that interfere with uncharged tRNA-binding in vitro abolished GCN2 activity in yeast (Wek et al., 1995; Zhu et al., 1996) and by evidence that tRNA binding to the HisRS-like portion of GCN2 relieves an intramolecular repressive signal arising from its interaction with the kinase domain (Dong et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wek et al., 1995 and Zhu et al., 1996.

claim: tRNA binding to the HisRS-like portion of GCN2 relieves an intramolecular repressive signal arising from its interaction with the kinase domain.
source: This model was supported by the observations that mutations in the HisRS-like module that interfere with uncharged tRNA-binding in vitro abolished GCN2 activity in yeast (Wek et al., 1995; Zhu et al., 1996) and by evidence that tRNA binding to the HisRS-like portion of GCN2 relieves an intramolecular repressive signal arising from its interaction with the kinase domain (Dong et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dong et al., 2000.

claim: GCN2 activity relies on direct interactions with ribosomes or ribosome-associated proteins.
source: Parallel lines of enquiry indicate that GCN2 activity also relies on direct (Ramirez et al., 1991; Zhu and Wek, 1998) and indirect (Marton et al., 1997) interactions with ribosomes or ribosome-associated proteins (Jiménez-Díaz et al., 2013; Inglis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ramirez et al., 1991; Zhu and Wek, 1998; Marton et al., 1997; Jiménez-Díaz et al., 2013; and Inglis et al., 2019.

claim: GCN2 activity relies on indirect interactions with ribosomes or ribosome-associated proteins.
source: Parallel lines of enquiry indicate that GCN2 activity also relies on direct (Ramirez et al., 1991; Zhu and Wek, 1998) and indirect (Marton et al., 1997) interactions with ribosomes or ribosome-associated proteins (Jiménez-Díaz et al., 2013; Inglis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Marton et al., 1997; Jiménez-Díaz et al., 2013; and Inglis et al., 2019.

claim: GCN2 activation may not arise solely by binary interaction between GCN2 and uncharged tRNAs as activating ligands.
source: These latter observations suggest that GCN2 activation may not arise solely by binary interaction between GCN2 and uncharged tRNAs as activating ligands.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited ribosome interaction studies.

claim: A strain of mice (C57BL/6J) that lacks an abundant neuron-specific isoacceptor arginyl-tRNA has higher levels of GCN2-dependent ISR activity in brain tissues compared with a reference strain that expressed normal levels of the neuron-specific arginyl-tRNA.
source: A strain of mice (C57BL/6J) that lacks an abundant neuron-specific isoacceptor arginyl-tRNA was noted to have higher levels of GCN2-dependent ISR activity in brain tissues compared with a reference strain that expressed normal levels of the neuron-specific arginyl-tRNA.
evidence: This is a genetic observation from mice, as described in the introduction referencing Ishimura et al., 2016.

claim: ISR activity in arginyl-tRNA depleted C57BL/6J brain was not associated with globally elevated uncharged tRNAs.
source: ISR activity in arginyl-tRNA depleted C57BL/6J brain was not associated with globally elevated uncharged tRNAs, but was increased by a second mutation that compromises the cells ability to re-cycle stalled ribosomes (Ishimura et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ishimura et al., 2016.

claim: ISR activity in arginyl-tRNA depleted C57BL/6J brain was increased by a second mutation that compromises the cells ability to re-cycle stalled ribosomes.
source: ISR activity in arginyl-tRNA depleted C57BL/6J brain was not associated with globally elevated uncharged tRNAs, but was increased by a second mutation that compromises the cells ability to re-cycle stalled ribosomes (Ishimura et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ishimura et al., 2016.

claim: A mechanism for activating mammalian GCN2 emanates from a (stalled) ribosome-generated signal that arises when pools of charged tRNAs are limiting.
source: Together, these observations suggest a mechanism for activating mammalian GCN2 that emanates from a (stalled) ribosome-generated signal that arises when pools of charged tRNAs are limiting.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observations about C57BL/6J mice.

claim: GCN2 activation may proceed independently of globally elevated levels of uncharged tRNAs.
source: Whilst a role for localized pools of uncharged tRNAs remains possible, the findings of Ishimura (et al. 2016) suggest that GCN2 activation may proceed independently of globally elevated levels of uncharged tRNAs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the findings of Ishimura et al., 2016.

claim: In both HeLa and CHO cells inactivation of the GCN2-encoding Eif2ak4 gene selectively abolished responsiveness of the ISR regulated CHOP::GFP reporter to the histidinyl-tRNA synthetase inhibitor, histidinol.
source: In both HeLa and CHO cells inactivation of the GCN2-encoding Eif2ak4 gene selectively abolished responsiveness of the ISR regulated CHOP::GFP reporter to the histidinyl-tRNA synthetase inhibitor, histidinol.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the flow cytometry data in Figure 1A and B.

claim: In both HeLa and CHO cells with Eif2ak4 inactivation, the CHOP::GFP reporter remained responsive to the glycosylation inhibitor tunicamycin.
source: In both cell lines, the CHOP::GFP reporter remained responsive to the glycosylation inhibitor tunicamycin, a toxin that activates the ISR orthogonally, through an ER stress inducible eIF2α kinase, PERK (Figure 1A and B). (Harding et al., 1999; Harding et al., 2000).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the flow cytometry data in Figure 1A and B, and supported by citations to Harding et al., 1999 and Harding et al., 2000.

claim: Tunicamycin activates the ISR orthogonally, through an ER stress inducible eIF2α kinase, PERK.
source: In both cell lines, the CHOP::GFP reporter remained responsive to the glycosylation inhibitor tunicamycin, a toxin that activates the ISR orthogonally, through an ER stress inducible eIF2α kinase, PERK (Figure 1A and B). (Harding et al., 1999; Harding et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Harding et al., 1999 and Harding et al., 2000.

claim: GCN2 ablation did not affect the tunicamycin-responsive XBP1::mCherry reporter present in the CHO cells.
source: Furthermore, GCN2 ablation did not affect the tunicamycin-responsive XBP1::mCherry reporter present in the CHO cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the flow cytometry data in Figure 1B.

claim: Guides targeting Eif2ak4 were amongst the most highly enriched in the CHOP::GFP dull cells after two rounds of sorting.
source: After two rounds of sorting, sequencing of the guides confirmed that those targeting the GCN2 encoding Eif2ak4 were amongst the most highly enriched in the dull cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sequencing data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Ontology cluster analysis revealed enrichment for guides targeting the mRNA cap binding complex, other translation initiation factors, and ribosomal proteins in the CHOP::GFP dull cells.
source: Ontology cluster analysis also revealed enrichment for guides targeting the mRNA cap binding complex, other translation initiation factors, and ribosomal proteins, consistent with similar studies previously carried out in yeast (Hinnebusch, 2005).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the screening data, with reference to similar yeast studies.

claim: Many of the HeLa cells selected for CHOP::GFP dullness had also lost the ability to respond to tunicamycin.
source: Despite the enrichment for guides targeting genes plausibly implicated in amino acid starvation-mediated ISR activation, many of the HeLa cells selected for CHOP::GFP dullness had also lost the ability to respond to tunicamycin (not shown).
evidence: This is an observation from the HeLa screen that is stated but not shown.

claim: The clonogenic potential of stressed HeLa cells was poor, compared with CHO cells.
source: Furthermore, it became evident that the clonogenic potential of stressed HeLa cells was poor, compared with CHO cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the crystal violet staining shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Guides targeting Rps10 (encoding eS10) were enriched in the dull CHO cells.
source: Among the latter was Rps10 (encoding eS10), previously implicated in GCN2 responsiveness to amino acid starvation in yeast (Lee et al., 2015) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sequencing data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, and supported by citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claim: Guides targeting Rplp0 and Rplp1, encoding uL10 and P1, both components of the acidic ribosomal P-stalk, were conspicuously enriched in the dull CHO cells.
source: Guides targeting two other ribosomal genes were also conspicuously enriched in the dull CHO cells: Rplp0 and Rplp1, encoding uL10 and P1, both components of the acidic ribosomal P-stalk, a heteropentameric structure that also includes P2 (guides directed to the P2-encoding Rplp2 gene were also modestly enriched in the dull population) (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sequencing data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Guides directed to the P2-encoding Rplp2 gene were modestly enriched in the dull population.
source: Guides targeting two other ribosomal genes were also conspicuously enriched in the dull CHO cells: Rplp0 and Rplp1, encoding uL10 and P1, both components of the acidic ribosomal P-stalk, a heteropentameric structure that also includes P2 (guides directed to the P2-encoding Rplp2 gene were also modestly enriched in the dull population) (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sequencing data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The enriched Rplp0 guides mapped to the region encoding the C-terminus of uL10, which constitutes the helical spine of the P-stalk protrusion from the ribosome surface and the linker connecting it to the ribosome core.
source: The enriched Rplp0 guides caught our interest, because they mapped to the region encoding the C-terminus of uL10, which constitutes the helical spine of the P-stalk protrusion from the ribosome surface and the linker connecting it to the ribosome core.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the guide sequences and structural knowledge, as illustrated in Figure 1F.

claim: Guides targeting the ribosome-embedded N-terminal portion of uL10 were strongly depleted from all pools of CHO cells (regardless of their ISR status).
source: Guides targeting the ribosome-embedded N-terminal portion of uL10 were strongly depleted from all pools of CHO cells (regardless of their ISR status) consistent with a role for this portion of the protein in cell fitness (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sequencing data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: The N-terminal portion of uL10 plays a role in cell fitness.
source: Guides targeting the ribosome-embedded N-terminal portion of uL10 were strongly depleted from all pools of CHO cells (regardless of their ISR status) consistent with a role for this portion of the protein in cell fitness (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is inferred from the depletion of guides targeting this region.

claim: Histidinol induction of CHOP::GFP expression was conspicuously compromised in CHO cells targeted with Rplp0 and Rplp1 guides found to be enriched in CHOP::GFP dull cells.
source: Histidinol induction of CHOP::GFP expression was conspicuously compromised in the targeted clones, whereas their responsiveness to ER stress-inducing agents was unaffected.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the flow cytometry data in Figure 2A.

claim: Rplp0 and Rplp1 mutant cells retained responsiveness to ER stress-inducing agents.
source: Histidinol induction of CHOP::GFP expression was conspicuously compromised in the targeted clones, whereas their responsiveness to ER stress-inducing agents was unaffected.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the flow cytometry data in Figure 2A.

claim: A selective defect was observed in Rplp0 and Rplp1 mutant cells in response to lysine and arginine depletion, albeit not to the level of GCN2 ablated cells.
source: A selective defect was also observed in Rplp0 and Rplp1 mutant cells in response to lysine and arginine depletion, albeit not to the level of GCN2 ablated cells (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the flow cytometry data in Figure 2A and B.

claim: The defect in the ISR brought about by targeting cells with the Rplp0-directed guide was rescued by restoring gene function through re-targeting the mutant Rplp0 locus with a homologous repair template.
source: The defect in the ISR brought about by targeting cells with the Rplp0-directed guide was rescued by restoring gene function, attained by re-targeting the mutant Rplp0 locus with a homologous repair template to reestablish the coding region of the gene (whilst adding an epitope tag) (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the flow cytometry and immunoblot data in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Amino acid starvation of wildtype cells resulted in redistribution of ribosomes from denser polysome fractions to lighter fractions and to free 40S and 60S subunits.
source: Amino acid starvation of wildtype cells resulted in the expected redistribution of ribosomes from denser polysome fractions to lighter fractions and to free 40S and 60S subunits.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the polysome profile data in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The starvation-induced shift in the ribosome profile was lost in GCN2-ablated cells.
source: This starvation-induced shift in the ribosome profile was lost in GCN2-ablated cells, but only partially attenuated even in the strongest single mutant lines (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the polysome profile data in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The starvation-induced shift in the ribosome profile was only partially attenuated in the strongest single P-stalk mutant lines.
source: This starvation-induced shift in the ribosome profile was lost in GCN2-ablated cells, but only partially attenuated even in the strongest single mutant lines (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the polysome profile data in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The compound P-stalk Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 double mutant cells phenocopied GCN2 ablation in terms of polysome profile.
source: In an effort to acquire a more penetrant lesion in the P-stalk, we targeted several Rplp0 mutant clones with guides to Rplp1. Very few double mutant cells survived the procedure, but one such clone Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 (encoding a uL10 truncated at Y231 and a P1 protein lacking H17-D18 in helix 1) phenocopied GCN2 ablation both in terms of its polysome profile and activation of the CHOP::GFP reporter (Figure 3A–3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the polysome profile data in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The compound P-stalk Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 double mutant cells phenocopied GCN2 ablation in terms of activation of the CHOP::GFP reporter.
source: In an effort to acquire a more penetrant lesion in the P-stalk, we targeted several Rplp0 mutant clones with guides to Rplp1. Very few double mutant cells survived the procedure, but one such clone Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 (encoding a uL10 truncated at Y231 and a P1 protein lacking H17-D18 in helix 1) phenocopied GCN2 ablation both in terms of its polysome profile and activation of the CHOP::GFP reporter (Figure 3A–3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the flow cytometry data in Figure 3C.

claim: In wildtype cells amino-acid starvation led to a time dependent accumulation of activated hyper-phosphorylated GCN2.
source: In wildtype cells amino-acid starvation led to a time dependent accumulation of activated hyper-phosphorylated GCN2, which was conspicuously lacking in the Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the PhosTag gel data in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Activated hyper-phosphorylated GCN2 was conspicuously lacking in the Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 cells following amino-acid starvation.
source: In wildtype cells amino-acid starvation led to a time dependent accumulation of activated hyper-phosphorylated GCN2, which was conspicuously lacking in the Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the PhosTag gel data in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The heterogenous mobility shift of GCN2 from starved wild type cells reflected multiple phosphorylation events.
source: Phosphatase treatment of the lysate, prior to gel loading, confirmed that the heterogenous mobility shift indeed reflected multiple phosphorylation events (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the phosphatase treatment experiment in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The compound P-stalk Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 double mutant cells were selectively defective in induction of the endogenous ISR markers CHOP and ATF4 in response to amino acid starvation.
source: Like the GCN2 ablated cells, the compound P-stalk Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 double mutant cells were also selectively defective in induction of the endogenous ISR markers CHOP and ATF4 in response to amino acid starvation but retained inducibility of the markers to ER stress (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the immunoblot data in Figure 3F.

claim: The compound P-stalk Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 double mutant cells retained inducibility of CHOP and ATF4 to ER stress.
source: Like the GCN2 ablated cells, the compound P-stalk Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 double mutant cells were also selectively defective in induction of the endogenous ISR markers CHOP and ATF4 in response to amino acid starvation but retained inducibility of the markers to ER stress (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the immunoblot data in Figure 3F.

claim: Ribosomes isolated from the Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 double mutant cells had diminished P1/P2 content.
source: Furthermore, ribosomes isolated from the mutant cells had diminished P1/P2 content (conspicuous in the Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 double mutant but also apparent in the Rplp0m14 single mutant (Figure 4B, middle panel), consistent with a destabilizing effect of the mutations on the association of P1 and P2 with the ribosome.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the Coomassie-stained gel and immunoblot data in Figure 4B.

claim: The mutations in uL10 have a destabilizing effect on the association of P1 and P2 with the ribosome.
source: Furthermore, ribosomes isolated from the mutant cells had diminished P1/P2 content (conspicuous in the Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 double mutant but also apparent in the Rplp0m14 single mutant (Figure 4B, middle panel), consistent with a destabilizing effect of the mutations on the association of P1 and P2 with the ribosome.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of diminished P1/P2 content in ribosomes from mutant cells.

claim: Intact ribosomes can stimulate GCN2-mediated phosphorylation of eIF2α in vitro.
source: While these studies were ongoing, we learned of findings, now published, indicating a physical interaction between GCN2 and the mammalian ribosomal P-stalk and providing evidence that intact ribosomes, or their isolated P-stalk, can stimulate GCN2-mediated phosphorylation of eIF2α in vitro (Inglis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Inglis et al., 2019.

claim: Isolated P-stalk can stimulate GCN2-mediated phosphorylation of eIF2α in vitro.
source: While these studies were ongoing, we learned of findings, now published, indicating a physical interaction between GCN2 and the mammalian ribosomal P-stalk and providing evidence that intact ribosomes, or their isolated P-stalk, can stimulate GCN2-mediated phosphorylation of eIF2α in vitro (Inglis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Inglis et al., 2019.

claim: There is a physical interaction between GCN2 and the mammalian ribosomal P-stalk.
source: While these studies were ongoing, we learned of findings, now published, indicating a physical interaction between GCN2 and the mammalian ribosomal P-stalk and providing evidence that intact ribosomes, or their isolated P-stalk, can stimulate GCN2-mediated phosphorylation of eIF2α in vitro (Inglis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Inglis et al., 2019.

claim: At the concentrations used, isolated ribosomes had negligible associated eIF2α kinase activity.
source: At the concentrations used, isolated ribosomes had negligible associated eIF2α kinase activity.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 5.

claim: Nanomolar concentration of ribosomes isolated from wildtype CHO cells markedly stimulated eIF2α phosphorylation by GCN2.
source: However, in our hands too, nanomolar concentration of ribosomes isolated from wildtype CHO cells markedly stimulated eIF2α phosphorylation by GCN2 (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Ribosomes isolated from the Rplp0 and compound Rplp0/Rplp1 mutant cells were impaired in GCN2-dependent eIF2α phosphorylation.
source: Interestingly, ribosomes isolated from the Rplp0 and compound Rplp0/Rplp1 mutant cells were impaired in GCN2-dependent eIF2α phosphorylation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the in vitro kinase assays shown in Figure 5A-C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: The hierarchy of the defect in GCN2 activation by the different ribosome preparations in vitro correlated with the ISR impairment of their source mutant cells in vivo.
source: Furthermore, the hierarchy of the defect in GCN2 activation by the different ribosome preparations in vitro correlated with the ISR impairment of their source mutant cells in vivo, in that the in vitro defect was more severe in preparations of ribosomes from compound Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 mutant cells than its Rplp0m9 single mutant parent or the unrelated Rplp0m14 single mutant (Figure 5A–5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing the in vitro kinase assays in Figure 5A-C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C with the cellular phenotypes.

claim: The stimulatory effect of ribosomes on eIF2α phosphorylation appeared to be GCN2 specific.
source: The stimulatory effect of ribosomes appeared to be GCN2 specific, as the related PERK kinase was only minimally activated in vitro (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the in vitro kinase assays comparing GCN2 and PERK in Figure 6A.

claim: The related PERK kinase was only minimally activated by ribosomes in vitro.
source: The stimulatory effect of ribosomes appeared to be GCN2 specific, as the related PERK kinase was only minimally activated in vitro (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the in vitro kinase assays in Figure 6A.

claim: The lack of effect of P-stalk lesions on the PERK-dependent ISR induction by ER stress in cells is consistent with the minimal activation of PERK by ribosomes in vitro.
source: This finding is consistent with the lack of effect of the P-stalk lesions on the PERK-dependent ISR induction by ER stress in cells (Figures 2A and 3B–3F).
evidence: This is an inference connecting the in vitro and in vivo observations.

claim: At physiological substrate concentrations of 2 µM eIF2α, the approximately 10-fold increase in the rate of GCN2-dependent eIF2α phosphorylation brought about by the presence of wildtype ribosomes could be mimicked by a 10-fold increase in the concentration of GCN2 in in vitro reactions without ribosomes.
source: At physiological substrate concentrations of 2 µM eIF2α (Chen et al., 2015), the approximately 10-fold increase in the rate of GCN2-dependent eIF2α phosphorylation brought about by the presence of wildtype ribosomes (Figure 5C) could be mimicked by a 10-fold increase in the concentration of GCN2 in in vitro reactions without ribosomes.
evidence: This is based on comparison of reaction rates from the in vitro kinase assays, with citation to Chen et al., 2015 for the physiological substrate concentration.

claim: The relationship between reaction velocity and substrate concentration proved very different when comparing GCN2 (2.5 nM) with ribosomes (50 nM) to GCN2 alone (at 25 nM).
source: However, the relationship between reaction velocity and substrate concentration proved very different when comparing GCN2 (2.5 nM) with ribosomes (50 nM) to GCN2 alone (at 25 nM).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the kinetic analysis shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: GCN2 with ribosomes saturates at less than 50 μM substrate with a Km of ~7.8 µM and a Vmax of 130 min−1.
source: While the former reaction saturates at less than 50 μM (substrate Km of ~7.8 µM (95% confidence 5.2–10.4 µM) and a Vmax of 130 min−1 (95% confidence 116–140 min−1)) the latter reaction was not saturated with substrate concentrations attainable experimentally (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the kinetic analysis shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: GCN2 alone was not saturated with substrate concentrations attainable experimentally.
source: While the former reaction saturates at less than 50 μM (substrate Km of ~7.8 µM (95% confidence 5.2–10.4 µM) and a Vmax of 130 min−1 (95% confidence 116–140 min−1)) the latter reaction was not saturated with substrate concentrations attainable experimentally (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the kinetic analysis shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: The kinetic properties of GCN2, reacted with ribosomes from the mutant Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 cells, resembled GCN2 alone.
source: The kinetic properties of GCN2, reacted with ribosomes from the mutant Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 cells, resembled GCN2 alone, establishing a role for the P-stalk in this shift in the enzymatic properties of the kinase (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the kinetic analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The P-stalk plays a role in the shift in the enzymatic properties of GCN2.
source: The kinetic properties of GCN2, reacted with ribosomes from the mutant Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 cells, resembled GCN2 alone, establishing a role for the P-stalk in this shift in the enzymatic properties of the kinase (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of kinetic properties with wildtype and mutant ribosomes.

claim: Ribosome-mediated potentiation of GCN2's eIF2α-directed kinase activity was not associated with a consistent difference in the known GCN2 auto-activation mark, phosphorylation of activation-loop residue Thr899.
source: In keeping with recent observation (Inglis, 2018 and Inglis et al., 2019), we also noted that ribosome-mediated potentiation of GCN2's eIF2α-directed kinase activity was not associated with a consistent difference in the known GCN2 auto-activation mark, phosphorylation of activation-loop residue Thr899 (Romano et al., 1998) (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the immunoblot data in Figure 6D, and supported by citations to Inglis, 2018; Inglis et al., 2019; and Romano et al., 1998.

claim: In vitro, ribosomes promote GCN2 phosphorylation on residues other than threonine 899.
source: It is noteworthy that in vitro, ribosomes promote GCN2 phosphorylation on residues other than threonine 899 (Inglis, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Inglis, 2018.

claim: The phos-tag gels report on multiple phosphorylation events in the amino acid deprived wildtype cells that are absent from P-stalk mutant cells.
source: However, given that the phos-tag gels report on multiple phosphorylation events in the amino acid deprived wildtype cells that are absent from P-stalk mutant cells, it seems reasonable to conclude that the ribosome-mediated signal also results in phosphorylating events other than pThr899 in vivo.
evidence: This is based on the PhosTag gel data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: The ribosome-mediated signal results in phosphorylating events other than pThr899 in vivo.
source: However, given that the phos-tag gels report on multiple phosphorylation events in the amino acid deprived wildtype cells that are absent from P-stalk mutant cells, it seems reasonable to conclude that the ribosome-mediated signal also results in phosphorylating events other than pThr899 in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the PhosTag gel data.

claim: Mammalian ribosomes imparted on GCN2 new enzymatic properties, reflected in the lowering of the enzymes Km.
source: Nonetheless, mammalian ribosomes imparted on GCN2 new enzymatic properties, reflected in the lowering of the enzymes Km.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the kinetic analysis shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: The correlation between a selective defect in GCN2-mediated ISR activation in cells with genetic lesions to their P-stalk and a defect in ability of their ribosomes to activate GCN2 in vitro implicates the P-stalk in propagating a signal from ribosomes perturbed by amino acid starvation to GCN2.
source: The correlation, established here, between a selective defect in GCN2-mediated ISR activation in cells with genetic lesions to their P-stalk and a defect in ability of their ribosomes to activate GCN2 in vitro implicates the P-stalk in propagating a signal from ribosomes perturbed by amino acid starvation to GCN2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined in vivo and in vitro data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The location of the P-stalk on the surface of the ribosome is adjacent to the A site.
source: The location of the P-stalk on the surface of the ribosome adjacent to the A site and its functional role in recruiting elongation factors to the ribosome (Helgstrand et al., 2007; Nomura et al., 2012) and in stimulating their GTPase activity (Mohr et al., 2002), implicate the P-stalk in translation elongation.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: The P-stalk has a functional role in recruiting elongation factors to the ribosome.
source: The location of the P-stalk on the surface of the ribosome adjacent to the A site and its functional role in recruiting elongation factors to the ribosome (Helgstrand et al., 2007; Nomura et al., 2012) and in stimulating their GTPase activity (Mohr et al., 2002), implicate the P-stalk in translation elongation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Helgstrand et al., 2007 and Nomura et al., 2012.

claim: The P-stalk has a functional role in stimulating the GTPase activity of elongation factors.
source: The location of the P-stalk on the surface of the ribosome adjacent to the A site and its functional role in recruiting elongation factors to the ribosome (Helgstrand et al., 2007; Nomura et al., 2012) and in stimulating their GTPase activity (Mohr et al., 2002), implicate the P-stalk in translation elongation.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mohr et al., 2002.

claim: The P-stalk is implicated in translation elongation.
source: The location of the P-stalk on the surface of the ribosome adjacent to the A site and its functional role in recruiting elongation factors to the ribosome (Helgstrand et al., 2007; Nomura et al., 2012) and in stimulating their GTPase activity (Mohr et al., 2002), implicate the P-stalk in translation elongation.
evidence: This is inferred from the P-stalk's location and functional roles.

claim: In elongating ribosomes, charged cognate tRNAs (in complex with eEF1A) followed by eEF2, cycle through the A site.
source: In elongating ribosomes, charged cognate tRNAs (in complex with eEF1A) followed by eEF2, cycle through the A site (reviewed in Brown and Shao, 2018; Dever et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about translation elongation, supported by citations to Brown and Shao, 2018 and Dever et al., 2018.

claim: The cycling of elongation factors in proximity to the P-stalk may restrain the P-stalk's GCN2 stimulatory activity.
source: It is tempting to speculate on a scenario whereby the cycling of these factors in proximity to the P-stalk restrains the latter's GCN2 stimulatory activity.
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed by the authors.

claim: Elongation factor mediated steric blocking of the interaction between GCN2 and domain II of uL10 may restrain the P-stalk's GCN2 stimulatory activity.
source: This may occur through elongation factor mediated steric blocking of the interaction between GCN2 and domain II of uL10 (shown to be essential for GCN2-P-Stalk binding, Inglis et al., 2019), by competition for the attention of the acidic C-terminal tails of the P-stalk proteins (which are important for activation of GCN2, Inglis et al., 2019), or by eliciting conformational changes in the P-stalk.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism proposed by the authors, with reference to Inglis et al., 2019.

claim: Competition for the acidic C-terminal tails of the P-stalk proteins may restrain the P-stalk's GCN2 stimulatory activity.
source: This may occur through elongation factor mediated steric blocking of the interaction between GCN2 and domain II of uL10 (shown to be essential for GCN2-P-Stalk binding, Inglis et al., 2019), by competition for the attention of the acidic C-terminal tails of the P-stalk proteins (which are important for activation of GCN2, Inglis et al., 2019), or by eliciting conformational changes in the P-stalk.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism proposed by the authors, with reference to Inglis et al., 2019.

claim: Elongation factors eliciting conformational changes in the P-stalk may restrain the P-stalk's GCN2 stimulatory activity.
source: This may occur through elongation factor mediated steric blocking of the interaction between GCN2 and domain II of uL10 (shown to be essential for GCN2-P-Stalk binding, Inglis et al., 2019), by competition for the attention of the acidic C-terminal tails of the P-stalk proteins (which are important for activation of GCN2, Inglis et al., 2019), or by eliciting conformational changes in the P-stalk.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism proposed by the authors.

claim: Disruption of the elongation cycle by lack of cognate charged tRNA stalls ribosomes in a conformation that relieves restraint(s) on the P-stalk, exposing the dormant capacity of the P-stalk to activate GCN2.
source: Disruption of this elongation cycle by lack of cognate charged tRNA presumably stalls ribosomes in a conformation that relieves such restraint(s), exposing the dormant capacity of the P-stalk to activate GCN2 (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed by the authors, illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: Ribosomes isolated from actively-translating fed cells were potent activators of GCN2 in vitro.
source: Ribosomes isolated from actively-translating fed cells (with repressed GCN2), were nonetheless potent activators of GCN2 in vitro (our observation and Inglis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is based on the in vitro kinase assays presented in the manuscript and supported by citation to Inglis et al., 2019.

claim: Ribosome isolation disrupts the constraints on the P-stalk and exposes its latent ability to activate the kinase in vitro.
source: Presumably ribosome isolation disrupts the aforementioned constraints on the P-stalk and exposes its latent ability to activate the kinase in vitro.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the in vitro observations.

claim: Activation by the mammalian P-stalk requires both the ribosome-associated N-terminal domain II of uL10 and the acidic C-termini of the three P-stalk components that extend from the ribosomes surface.
source: Activation by the mammalian P-stalk requires both the ribosome-associated N-terminal domain II of uL10 and the acidic C-termini of the three P-stalk components that extend from the ribosomes surface (Inglis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Inglis et al., 2019.

claim: The yeast P1/P2 proteins are sufficient for GCN2 activation in vitro.
source: By contrast, the yeast P1/P2 proteins are sufficient for GCN2 activation in vitro (Jiménez-Díaz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiménez-Díaz et al., 2013.

claim: The free pool of yeast P2 contributes to GCN2 activation in response to osmotic stress and glucose deprivation.
source: Interestingly, the free pool of yeast P2 contributes to GCN2 activation in response to osmotic stress and glucose deprivation, but is dispensable for GCN2 activation by histidine depletion.
evidence: This is based on genetic evidence from yeast studies, as discussed in the context of Jiménez-Díaz et al., 2013.

claim: The free pool of yeast P2 is dispensable for GCN2 activation by histidine depletion.
source: Interestingly, the free pool of yeast P2 contributes to GCN2 activation in response to osmotic stress and glucose deprivation, but is dispensable for GCN2 activation by histidine depletion.
evidence: This is based on genetic evidence from yeast studies, as discussed in the context of Jiménez-Díaz et al., 2013.

claim: GCN2's response to amino acid starvation might depend on a ribosome-coupled P-stalk mediated signal, which may be provided adequately by yeast uL10 even in the absence of associated P1/P2.
source: The latter observation is consistent with the notion that GCN2's response to amino acid starvation might depend on a ribosome-coupled P-stalk mediated signal, which may be provided adequately by yeast uL10 even in the absence of associated P1/P2 (Jiménez-Díaz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the yeast data, with reference to Jiménez-Díaz et al., 2013.

claim: The importance of the physical coupling between the P-stalk and the ribosome to mammalian GCN2 activation is suggested by the strong phenotype of the compound Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 mutant.
source: The importance of the physical coupling between the P-stalk and the ribosome to mammalian GCN2 activation is suggested by the strong phenotype of the compound Rplp0/Rplp1m29-132 mutant in which the truncation of uL10 and the internal deletion of P1 conspire to deplete ribosomes of associated P-stalk acidic C-termini, whilst retaining a substantial pool of cytosolic P proteins with intact C-termini.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotype of the compound mutant.

claim: Efficient delivery of the P-stalk's message to GCN2 relies on proximity to the ribosome.
source: The notion that efficient delivery of the P-stalk's message to GCN2 relies on proximity to the ribosome is consistent with the importance of other contacts made between GCN2 and the mammalian ribosome, such as those dependent on eS10 (Lee et al., 2015) (a product of a gene also 'hit' in our screen for CHOP::GFP dull cells).
evidence: This is inferred from the genetic data and supported by citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claim: In mammals there may be a role for the free pool of P1/P2 proteins in GCN2 activation in response to other non-ribosomal stress signals.
source: Whilst the ribosome takes central stage in GCN2 activation by amino acid starvation, it is interesting to consider that in mammals too there may be a role for the free pool of P1/P2 proteins in GCN2 activation in response to other non-ribosomal stress signals.
evidence: This is a speculative consideration by the authors.

claim: Yeast P1/P2 proteins markedly stimulated GCN2 autophosphorylation in vitro.
source: Yeast P1/P2 proteins markedly stimulated GCN2 autophosphorylation in vitro (Jiménez-Díaz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiménez-Díaz et al., 2013.

claim: Mammalian ribosomes had no consistent effect on the phosphorylation status of GCN2 Thr899.
source: However, mammalian ribosomes had no consistent effect on the phosphorylation status of GCN2 Thr899 (here, Inglis, 2018 and Inglis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is based on the data presented in the manuscript and supported by citations to Inglis, 2018 and Inglis et al., 2019.

claim: The importance of GCN2's relationship with ribosomes to activation of the ISR was first recognized before identification of eIF2α as GCN2's substrate.
source: The importance of GCN2's relationship with ribosomes to activation of the ISR (known in yeast as the GCN4-dependent General Control gene expression program) was first recognized before identification of eIF2α as GCN2's substrate (Ramirez et al., 1991; Zhu and Wek, 1998) and subsequently buttressed by identification of ribosome-associated factors such as GCN1 and GCN20 as important GCN2 co-factors (Marton et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ramirez et al., 1991; Zhu and Wek, 1998; and Marton et al., 1997.

claim: GCN1 and GCN20 are ribosome-associated factors that are important GCN2 co-factors.
source: The importance of GCN2's relationship with ribosomes to activation of the ISR (known in yeast as the GCN4-dependent General Control gene expression program) was first recognized before identification of eIF2α as GCN2's substrate (Ramirez et al., 1991; Zhu and Wek, 1998) and subsequently buttressed by identification of ribosome-associated factors such as GCN1 and GCN20 as important GCN2 co-factors (Marton et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Marton et al., 1997.

claim: A stalled ribosome initiates a P-stalk-mediated activation signal for GCN2.
source: These seminal early findings, together with more recent work (of which this paper is part), point to a role for a stalled ribosome-initiated P-stalk-mediated activation signal.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined historical and current findings.

claim: GCN2, the first eIF2α kinase, may have evolved initially as part of a simple feed-back loop attenuating translation initiation in response to ribosome stalling.
source: Moreover, these observations suggest the possibility that GCN2, the first eIF2α kinase, evolved initially as part of a simple feed-back loop attenuating translation initiation in response to ribosome stalling.
evidence: This is a speculative evolutionary model proposed by the authors.

claim: The coupling of GCN2's activity to a gene expression program that acts physiologically to relieve some of the more common causes of stalling may have emerged later and eventually evolved into the ISR we recognize today in multicellular organism.
source: The coupling of GCN2's activity to a gene expression program that acts physiologically to relieve some of the more common causes of stalling, may have emerged later and eventually evolved into the ISR we recognize today in multicellular organism.
evidence: This is a speculative evolutionary model proposed by the authors.
